page: Amazon Web Services r6idn.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at up to 3.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, providing 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Compute resources are paired with 256 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. Storage and networking are hardware-accelerated, including 1,900 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. The instance does not include a dedicated GPU.

Benchmark evaluations position the r6idn.8xlarge consistently in the middle tier for compute and memory throughput. It achieves a Geekbench 6 multi-core score of 14,084, a single-core score of 1,656, and a PassMark CPU score of 36,566.42. Large-block memory bandwidth tests show 149.78 GB/sec for sequential reads and 68.42 GB/sec for writes. The system handles Redis SET operations at 31.23 million operations per second and static web throughput at 35.26 GB/sec. While text generation on small language models (135M) reaches a strong 307.77 tokens per second, large models such as 70B drop to 2.25 tokens per second due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

By bundling 1,900 GB of high-speed local NVMe storage directly with dense memory and a 50 Gbps network profile, the r6idn.8xlarge delivers high I/O throughput without requiring attached block storage volumes for scratch data. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of GPU acceleration, which limits extreme deep learning efficiency. Consequently, this server profile is best matched to memory-heavy relational databases, Redis caching layers, real-time analytics, and search indices requiring fast local disk access.
